title: The Fable 5.1 playbook.
lead: Fable 5.1 is Anthropic's most capable generally available model for coding and knowledge work. Here's how to point it at the right jobs, and the 10 highest-value ones to run first.
inside: Switch to Fable 5.1 in Claude Code, set the effort level per task, use the prompting rules that get the most out of it, and run 10 jobs worth the tokens.
what: Anthropic released Fable 5.1 on September 1, 2026. It's built for long, multi-step work: whole-codebase changes, deep analysis and sessions that run for hours. It defaults to High effort in Claude Code and Medium on claude.ai.
It costs more per token than Opus or Sonnet, so the move is to spend it on hard problems and on assets you build once and reuse, not on quick questions.
prereqs: A Claude plan or API account with Fable 5.1 access
Claude Code installed (for the build-once jobs)
One real problem you've been putting off
warn: Fable 5.1 is the expensive tier: $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output (cache reads dropped to $0.25). Some dual-use security tasks, like exploit generation, still get handed to Opus models. Use Sonnet for quick everyday asks and save Fable for the jobs below.

steps.p: In Claude Code, run /model and pick Fable 5.1. On claude.ai, pick it from the model menu. On the API the model id is claude-fable-5-1.

steps.h: Set the effort to the job
steps.p: Effort goes from low to max. High is the Claude Code default and fits most builds. Drop to medium for routine edits, where 5.1 matches the old model for less money. Go to xhigh or max only for the hardest problems.
Over-engineered prompts actually degrade the output. State the goal and the constraints, then stop. Let the model do the reasoning instead of scripting every step.
Give it the intent, not just the request. Knowing the "why" lets it make better judgment calls on the parts you didn't spell out.

steps.h: Let it run, and let it self-verify
steps.p: Fable can work for hours on one goal and check its own work with subagents. Give it room to run instead of interrupting every few minutes.

steps.h: Spend it on things you build once
steps.p: The best value is work that keeps paying: a brand system, a reorganized second brain, an auto-repurposing engine. Build it once with Fable 5.1, then run it daily on a cheaper model.

prompts.code: Make a checklist of every task I do in a normal day, then look at it and tell me exactly which of these you could automate for me and how.
Review all of the code that was written while you were unavailable and find every optimization and improvement, then implement the highest-impact ones.
Connect to the X MCP plus a trend-research skill and pull the 5 best ways people are actually using Fable 5 right now that fit my specific workflow.
Loop every 24 hours and run a full security check on all of my app's API endpoints, then report anything new that looks exposed or risky.
Here is my entire content library plus each post's metrics. Rank my true outliers and reverse-engineer the repeatable hook, structure, and topic patterns behind them.
Here is my website and my assets. Produce a complete brand guide (voice, colors, type, do's and don'ts) and lock it in as a reusable brand file I can hand to any tool.
Point yourself at my whole notes vault. Dedupe it, restructure it, cross-link it, and rebuild it into a clean memory system you can keep maintaining for me.
Here are my contracts, financials, and reports. Give me the redlines, pull the numbers straight from the tables, and make the strategic call a senior analyst would make.
Pull my numbers from every platform, including the ones with no public API, by running a headless browser to replay each site's hidden requests, then assemble one dashboard that refreshes daily.
Build me a Claude agent that repurposes and distributes each new post across all my channels while I sleep, and flags any cross-posting gaps it finds.
